questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
questions.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨\frac{1}{t},\,t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty )?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\sqrt{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+(1)^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}+1+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{1+{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}⟨-1,\,{t}^{2},\,\sqrt{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\frac{4}{t})\,j \\  & =\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{t})}^{2}+{(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{{t}^{2}}+{(1-\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{8}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{16}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}({t}^{4}+8{t}^{2}+16)} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}{({t}^{2}+4)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+4)}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{({t}^{2}+4)}(\frac{4}{t}\,i+(1-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}})\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)}(4t\,i+({t}^{2}-4)\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡2t+4{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}+\frac{3}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{3}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{4},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k$ at the point $P(2,1,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k & =2\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\,i+2\,j+\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{2}{3}\,j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=(t+{t}^{3})p(t)$ at the point where $t=1$, if $p(1)=\,i-2\,j+k$ and ${p}^{′}(1)=-2\,i+\,j+2\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+{t}^{3})p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+{t}^{3})p(t)+(t+{t}^{3})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(1+3{t}^{2})p(t)+(t+{t}^{3}){p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(1+3(1)^{2})p(1)+(1+{1}^{3}){p}^{′}(1) \\  & =4(i-2\,j+k)+2(-2\,i+\,j+2\,k) \\  & =-6j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+64} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(-6\,j+8\,k) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is $T(1)=-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{4}{5}\,k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=0$, given that  $p(0)=2\,i+j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(0)=i-2\,j-2\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2(0)}{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(0)+\frac{1}{{0}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =0(2\,i+j-k)+(\,i-2\,j-2k) \\  & =\,i-2\,j-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (i-2\,j-2\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is  $T(0)=\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={t}^{3}p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=-2\,i+\,j+\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=3\,i-3\,j+\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\cdot p(t)+{t}^{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,p(t)+{t}^{3}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =3(1)^{2}\,p(1)+(1)^{3}\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =3(-2\,i+\,j+\,k)+(3\,i-3\,j+\,k) \\  & =-6\,i+3\,j+3k+3\,i-3\,j+\,k \\  & =-3\,i+4\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-3\,i+4\,k) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,i+\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=-\frac{3}{5}\,i+\frac{4}{5}\,k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={e}^{-t}p(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, if $p(0)=\,i+\,j+k$ and ${p}^{′}(0)=\,i-\,j.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})p(t)+{e}^{-t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-{e}^{-t}p(t)+{e}^{-t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-{e}^{0}p(0)+{e}^{0}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =-(\,i+\,j+k)+(\,i-\,j) \\  & =-2j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(-2j-k) \\  & =-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $T(0)=-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$, given that  $p(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k$ and $\,{p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})=-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,p(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3})p(-\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3}){p}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,i+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(-2\,i-8\,j+4\,k) \\  & =(3\,i+3\,k)+(-\,i-4\,j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i-4\,j+5\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{r}^{′}(-\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot (2\,i-4\,j+5\,k) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ is
 $T(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\,i-\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k.$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \sin^3{t}, \:\cos^3{t} \right\rangle$ at an arbitrary point where $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)= x(t) \,\mathbf i + y(t) \,\mathbf j,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by 

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf r(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3{cos}^{2}⁡t(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\ \text{ } & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{1} \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the last step, we were able to remove the absolute value bars because $\sin{t}>0$ and $\cos{t}>0$ for $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=e^{2t}\mathbf p(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ if $\mathbf p(0)=\mathbf i-\,\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf p'(0)=\mathbf i - \mathbf j+ 2\mathbf k.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)=x(t)\mathbf i+y(t)\mathbf j+z(t)\mathbf k,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})p(t)+{e}^{2t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}p(t)+{e}^{2t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =2{e}^{2(0)}p(0)+{e}^{2(0)}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =2(i-\,j-k)+1(i-j+2k) \\  & =3\,i-3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot {3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}(3\,i-3\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $\mathbf T(0) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\mathbf i -  \mathbf j).$
